Re-review fixes 2026-10-11 (implementer summary, not reviewer-written; awaiting Astra's re-review of R1 and R2). R1: credentials.publish_anchor is the only anchor_write caller (boundary test); it takes the per-profile lock paths.anchor_lock (orders/.journal-anchor.lock), reads the journal head inside it and writes before releasing it, so the anchor never moves backwards; appends never take it. The kill publishes once, in close() after its sweep, waiting at most killswitch.JOURNAL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_S (2 s); a publication it cannot make is a stderr warning and never stops or delays a cancel. Other commands and resume wait at most credentials.ANCHOR_PUBLISH_WAIT_S (30 s; narrowed on 2026-10-12, next entry); new codes journal_anchor_publish_busy and journal_anchor_lock_unavailable. R2: paper_state schema_version 2 adds closed {markets: {market_id: closed_ms}, floor_ms}; a market seen CLOSED refuses paper place and replace and ignores every later book but a CLOSED one at or after its close (paper_market_closed); at most 256 markers are kept, and evicted closes raise floor_ms (paper_book_at_or_before_closed_floor); schema_version 1 states are still read and get their markers from the round-4 closing notes. R1 follow-up review 2026-10-12 (offline, r1-concurrency and r1-liveness lenses; implementer summary, not reviewer-written; not yet reviewed by Astra): 4 confirmed findings (1 major, 3 minor; two of the minor ones are one defect), all fixed, each with a regression test that fails on the reviewed candidate (v1n2/base) and on the tree before this round and passes now. (major) A journal restored in place to an older copy under a live session (sqlite3 ".restore", which every open connection then reads) was anchored by that session's next publication, after which the rolled-back journal passed A13 (base did the same; not introduced by R1): publish_anchor now also reads the Keychain anchor inside its lock and writes only a head that extends it under the A13 rule (arming.anchor_failures); otherwise journal_anchor_not_extended, nothing written, the anchor stays ahead and the next open refuses (journal_anchor_mismatch); an unreadable or invalid Keychain anchor writes nothing either. (minor x2) A lock path unlinked or replaced while the Keychain write ran let a second publisher write a newer head that this write could then overwrite while reporting success: held() is checked again after the write and the publication is made again under a freshly taken lock, at most credentials.ANCHOR_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS (3) times, then journal_anchor_lock_unavailable. (minor) Waiting for the anchor lock delayed manual cancels (a stuck kill close() or resume could hold a cancel's open() for 30 s while it held .gateway.lock): only a RISK_COMMANDS open() waits ANCHOR_PUBLISH_WAIT_S (30 s); cancel and reconcile open(), every close() and the kill wait killswitch.JOURNAL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_S (2 s); resume (no .gateway.lock) still waits 30 s. 77 facts (F01-F77): 76 recorded on 2026-10-10 and F77 added by the v1 live narrowing (an inference, no new source). 73 come from Betfair's own pages (documentation, policy, data specification and support articles, 3 of them via Wayback snapshots; F62 also has a secondary non-Betfair source), 3 from macOS man pages (F68, F73, F74) and 1 from a local Python check (F69); there are 2 local checks in all (F69, and F74's SQLite part, which F74's retrieval list and secondary inferred label carry). 3 are inferences (F67, F69, F77) and 6 are unverified (F30, F33, F36, F40, F56, F73). None has been checked against the live API. First-live tests T0-T10 need Yu's explicit go-ahead and presence (T11 was dropped with live replace).

v1 live surface narrowed by Yu's decision D1-D5 (2026-10-10; amendment-v1-live-scope.md in this directory): live place (LIMIT with LAPSE only), full cancels of our own bets, kill, live-probe (place then cancel), reconciling unknown outcomes and a new hand-typed settle-market. There is no live replace, no live partial cancel, no automatic live settlement (cleared rows never close or settle a live order; the operator settles a CLOSED market and each order is booked at its worst case) and no hedge credit in live risk limits. The kill never takes the gateway lock. F77, settle-market's premise, is inferred; a market Betfair no longer returns cannot be settled in v1 and stays counted at worst case (A20, decided by Yu on 2026-10-11: keep this conservative behaviour and settle soon after close; a possible forget-market only after the first-live T-tests with a fresh design and review, never in v1).
Live arming, the per-order tty echo and the Keychain dialog slow automation; they do not stop a deliberately malicious process running as Yu's macOS user.
Paper fills (paper-v1) are a conservative model, not execution evidence; delayed-key data cannot support features finer than 180 s.
The Live App Key (one-off 499 GBP) has not been bought; the delayed key can still place real bets, so key type is never treated as a safety control.

s0_patch:
--- a/AGENTS.md
+++ b/AGENTS.md
@@ -6,7 +6,8 @@
 - Record source URLs, access dates, publication dates where visible, commercial interests and limitations. Keep paraphrases short; do not archive full articles or conversations.
 - No profitable strategy has been established here. The inherited two-race pilot is descriptive and already inspected; it is not an untouched test set.
 - Keep chronology and data availability explicit. Target-race results, revised ratings and later prices cannot become earlier predictive inputs.
-- Current implementation scope includes public-source research, offline analysis and explicitly configured direct-feed collection on a small Fly deployment. There is no betting-account integration, executable betting strategy or live order path. Source policy, attribution, publication clocks and collection gaps must remain explicit.
+- Current implementation scope includes public-source research, offline analysis and explicitly configured direct-feed collection on a small Fly deployment. There is no executable betting strategy, and no strategy may submit orders automatically. Source policy, attribution, publication clocks and collection gaps must remain explicit.
+- `betangel_research/betfair` is a Betfair Exchange client: read-only market data, a stream recorder, and one order gateway that defaults to paper mode. Its live surface is limited to LIMIT orders with LAPSE persistence that the operator types at a terminal, cancelling our own bets, the kill switch, a one-pound live probe, reconciling unknown order outcomes and settling a closed market by hand; there is no live replace and no automatic live settlement. Live orders need every arming condition in docs/betfair-order-path.md. Betfair credentials live only in the macOS Keychain; the client certificate (default `~/.config/betangel-research/betfair/`) and live order state (`~/Library/Application Support/betangel-research/betfair/`) live outside every Git worktree.
 - Preserve the imported pilot as a provenance snapshot. Develop subsequent work separately; copy it to a temporary directory for reproduction checks.
 - Keep account exports, credentials and licensed raw data outside Git. Public visibility does not imply redistribution permission. Do not add a data licence on behalf of a provider.
 - Prefer Python standard library for simple analysis. Plotting has an optional pinned dependency in the pilot. Run proportionate checks and describe precisely what they establish.
